arms.label: Ember
evidence: 1. Overall form — 4/4: The hero and inset views clearly communicate the specified compact 7-inch wedge, sloped screen, rear plinth, and stable feet.

2. Display and controls — 3/4: The landscape tracker display and corrected five-button row are clear, but the specified recessed illuminated power button is not distinguishable from the tiny amber status light.
3. Native ports and power — 4/4: The final shows four USB-A plus Ethernet at right and, after correction, one USB-C plus two visibly differentiated micro-HDMI openings at the rear.
4. Airflow and fan direction — 4/4: The cutaway explicitly shows front-to-rear flow, separate upper and NVMe branches, heat transition, and outward rear exhaust through one fan.

5. Component-stack plausibility — 3/4: The display, Pi, upper cooling gap, lower NVMe board, standoffs, and base are coherently arranged, although the CPU cooler resembles a generic axial heatsink rather than the specified official Active Cooler.

6. Service features — 2/4: Screws, separable panels, and the exposed cutaway imply assembly access, but the captive rear hatch, bottom service plate, removable filter, and slide-out carrier are not clearly communicated.
7. Consistency across views — 4/4: Enclosure geometry, port locations, finishes, feet, intake, and rear structures remain consistent across the hero, rear, and cutaway views.
8. Absence of invented hardware — 3/4: Port and fan counts are disciplined and no fake audio hardware appears, but the generic cooler representation departs materially from the specified component.
9. Legibility and technical communication — 4/4: The three-view board, clear ports, airflow arrows, and internal cutaway provide the strongest technical explanation of the set.

10. Agreement with the final written design — 3/4: Most defining geometry, connectors, airflow, stack, and styling agree, with notable omissions or deviations in power-button treatment, cooler identity, and service provisions.

discrepancies.description: The recessed illuminated J2 power button specified by the written design is not visibly distinct; the image presents only a tiny amber light.
discrepancies.evidence: The design separately specifies a recessed illuminated normally-open power button, while the image prompt asks only for five keys and one tiny amber status light, and the delivered hero shows no separate power actuator.

discrepancies.description: The cutaway depicts a large generic square axial-fan heatsink rather than a recognizable Raspberry Pi official Active Cooler.
discrepancies.evidence: Both written design and prompt call for the Pi 5 with Active Cooler, but the cutaway shows a conventional top-mounted axial fan on a tall fin stack.

discrepancies.description: Specified service mechanisms are largely absent from the visual explanation.
discrepancies.evidence: The design calls for a captive-screw rear hatch and bottom plate, slide-out electronics carrier, and left-withdrawing filter; none is clearly identified in the final board.

arms.most_consequential_strength: The explicit cutaway and airflow arrows make the split cooling path and component stack unusually clear.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The image does not convincingly represent the specified official Active Cooler or the design's service mechanisms.

arms.label: Harbor
evidence: 1. Overall form — 4/4: The low 7-inch wedge, rear leveling heel, bronze rails, recessed display, feet, and continuous front grille form a coherent manufacturable product.
2. Display and controls — 4/4: The image clearly shows a landscape tracker display, exactly eight side-rail keys, a separate round power button, and an amber indicator.

3. Native ports and power — 3/4: Four USB-A, Ethernet, USB-C power, and two rear video openings are present, but the video openings read larger and less specifically micro-HDMI than required, and the separate display-power USB-C access is missing.
4. Airflow and fan direction — 3/4: A large open front intake and one guarded rear fan establish the intended path, but direction and upper/lower branch behavior remain implicit.
5. Component-stack plausibility — 2/4: The generous envelope could contain the described display, Pi/cooler, and NVMe stack, but no internal view or other evidence verifies the arrangement.
6. Service features — 2/4: Rear fasteners and grouped fan/cable areas suggest access, but the rear hatch, bottom sled, filter rail, microSD door, and replaceable display cassette are not legible.
7. Consistency across views — 4/4: The dark wedge, bronze rails, right-side port bank, rear heel, and feet remain coherent through all three views.
8. Absence of invented hardware — 4/4: No extra side ports, audio jacks, knobs, fans, or decorative hardware appear; the dark rear gutter corresponds to a requested cable-management feature.
9. Legibility and technical communication — 4/4: The spacious 16:9 composition gives clear hero, rear, and side-profile readings with well-resolved materials and connector pockets.

10. Agreement with the final written design — 3/4: Exterior form, controls, native port bank, fan, and visual language agree strongly, but display power access, internal stack, and service architecture are underrepresented.

discrepancies.description: The rear bay omits the additional accessible USB-C power connection required for the assumed display.
discrepancies.evidence: The written connector strategy separately requires native Pi USB-C power and accessible display USB-C power, while the exact image prompt requests only one USB-C inlet and the render shows one.

discrepancies.description: The two rear video openings are not convincingly rendered as the Pi's two micro-HDMI connectors.
discrepancies.evidence: The design identifies two native micro-HDMI openings, but the prompt weakens this to two generic 'HDMI-sized' openings and the image gives them full/mini-HDMI-like proportions.

discrepancies.description: The component stack and most routine service provisions are not demonstrated.
discrepancies.evidence: The design specifies an Active-Cooler/Pi/NVMe stack, display cassette, rear hatch, bottom sled, removable filter, and microSD door; the prompt prohibits cutaways and does not require these service details.

arms.most_consequential_strength: The exterior design, controls, port bank, stance, and repeated geometry are exceptionally coherent across views.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The rear connection scheme is incomplete for the design's separately powered display and visually ambiguous about micro-HDMI identity.

arms.label: Quartz
evidence: 1. Overall form — 4/4: The compact 4-inch wedge, tall rear heel, low front, metal spine, feet, and restrained shell closely match the specified proportions and character.
2. Display and controls — 4/4: The landscape interface is operator-correct and exactly five cream keys appear vertically on the left cheek as specified.
3. Native ports and power — 4/4: The side bay clearly contains four USB-A and Ethernet, while the rear inset shows USB-C, two differentiated HDMI openings, and the round native power actuator.

4. Airflow and fan direction — 3/4: Two unobstructed front intake bands and a single rear fan communicate front-to-rear cooling, but the internal split paths and exhaust direction are not explicitly shown.

5. Component-stack plausibility — 2/4: The compact enclosure appears capable of housing the proposed stack, but there is no direct evidence of display clearance, Active Cooler placement, or the under-Pi NVMe assembly.
6. Service features — 2/4: Part seams and rear captive fasteners are visible, but the bottom cassette, microSD door, fan/filter hatch, and serviceable filter are not clearly identifiable.
7. Consistency across views — 4/4: Shell shape, accent line, heel, feet, materials, rear hood, and fan placement remain consistent between hero and rear inset.

8. Absence of invented hardware — 4/4: The render avoids fake audio ports, knobs, duplicate fans, labels, or unsupported external hardware; the small side aperture corresponds to the requested cable-tie anchor.
9. Legibility and technical communication — 4/4: Both views are large, clean, and technically readable, with excellent separation of controls, intake, native ports, exhaust, and cable bay.

10. Agreement with the final written design — 4/4: All principal exterior decisions in the written design and exact prompt are represented with correct counts and placements; omissions primarily concern hidden internal and service details.

discrepancies.description: The internal display/Pi/Active-Cooler/NVMe stack and dual airflow channels are not visually verified.
discrepancies.evidence: The written design specifies detailed clearances and two flow paths, while the prompt requests only exterior hero and rear views and the final contains no cutaway.

discrepancies.description: Several specified service features remain visually ambiguous or absent.
discrepancies.evidence: The written design includes a two-screw microSD door, serviceable fan/filter hatch, removable bottom cassette, and side-removable filter; only general seams and rear screws are visible.

discrepancies.description: The side cable-tie feature resembles a small unidentified square port at first reading.
discrepancies.evidence: The prompt requests an adjacent reusable cable-tie slot, but the rendered feature is a solitary square recess without the geometry of an obvious strap or tie anchor.

arms.most_consequential_strength: It is the most literal and disciplined exterior translation of its written design, with correct control, port, power, intake, and exhaust counts.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The polished exterior board provides little evidence for the highly constrained internal stack and service architecture.

arms.label: Willow
evidence: 1. Overall form — 4/4: The broad 7-inch wedge, rear skirt, level feet, graphite finish, walnut rails, and sloped screen closely match the resolved form.

2. Display and controls — 2/4: The display is clear and correctly oriented, but the image shows nine visually identical keys rather than eight controller keys plus a clearly separated power key; it also violates the prompt's exact-eight constraint.
3. Native ports and power — 3/4: Four USB-A and Ethernet are correct, and the rear provides USB-C plus a plausible full-size HDMI service extension, but the front power control is not identifiable.
4. Airflow and fan direction — 3/4: The five-louver front intake and sole rear fan establish the intended route, although split flow and exhaust direction are only implied.
5. Component-stack plausibility — 2/4: The enclosure has ample apparent volume, but the decoupled display carrier and removable Pi/cooler/NVMe cassette are not demonstrated.
6. Service features — 1/4: The bottom service plate, top-carrier screws, removable filter, keyed cassette rails, and rear gallery cover are not visually communicated.
7. Consistency across views — 4/4: Form, walnut rails, finishes, side port position, feet, and rear geometry are highly consistent across the hero and two insets.

8. Absence of invented hardware — 3/4: External ports and fan count are disciplined, but the ninth identical key is extra relative to the exact prompt and lacks the design-required power-key distinction.
9. Legibility and technical communication — 3/4: Hero and connector details are clean and attractive, but control identity, service strategy, and internal architecture remain ambiguous.

10. Agreement with the final written design — 3/4: The form, materials, louvers, ports, rear fan, and total nine-control count broadly agree, but the separate power control and modular service architecture do not.

discrepancies.description: Nine identical front keys are rendered instead of eight controller keys plus a visually separated power key.
discrepancies.evidence: The written design clearly requires eight controller keys and a separate power key. The exact prompt instead demands exactly eight buttons, yet the renderer supplies nine without distinguishing power.

discrepancies.description: The written picture description inaccurately states that the generator prompt specified eight controller keys plus power control.
discrepancies.evidence: Willow-written-design.md section 5 makes that claim, while call-01.json explicitly says 'exactly eight' and contains no separate power-control instruction.

discrepancies.description: The prompt changes the written rear video strategy from a full-size HDMI panel extension to a micro-HDMI opening.
discrepancies.evidence: The written connector table specifies one rear full-size HDMI service output through an adapter, whereas the exact prompt requests one spare micro-HDMI opening; the render appears closer to full-size HDMI.

discrepancies.description: The decoupled component cassette and nearly all service mechanisms are omitted from the image.
discrepancies.evidence: The design specifies a removable Pi/cooler/NVMe cassette, replaceable top carrier, bottom service plate, filter, rear cover, and service fasteners, while the prompt requests only closed exterior views.

arms.most_consequential_strength: The enclosure's exterior form, material language, native side-port bank, louvers, and rear fan remain highly consistent across three polished views.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The control chain is internally contradictory and the delivered nine identical keys fail both the exact prompt and the design's required power-key distinction.

comparative_result: Quartz ranks first at 35/40 for the strongest literal exterior compliance and disciplined hardware counts. Ember follows at 34/40 and provides substantially better airflow and stack communication, but loses precision on the power button, cooler identity, and service features. Harbor scores 33/40 with excellent exterior coherence but an incomplete and ambiguous rear connection scheme. Willow scores 28/40 because its control count/identity chain is contradictory and its service architecture is largely absent.
disagreements: The closest judgment is Quartz versus Ember: Ember is clearly superior as a technical explanatory image, while Quartz is more faithful to its exact exterior specification and avoids Ember's incorrect cooler representation. Harbor is competitive on appearance and controls but not on rear power/video specificity. Willow's nine-button result matches the written design's total number of controls by accident, but not its required eight-plus-separated-power organization or the exact-eight prompt.
